text_blocks.snippet: The overall five-year survival rate for lung cancer is around 26.6%. This means that, on average, about 1 in 4 people diagnosed with lung cancer survive for at least five years. However, survival rates vary significantly based on the stage of the cancer at diagnosis, with early-stage diagnoses having much higher survival rates.
snippet_highlighted_words: The overall five-year survival rate for lung cancer is around 26.6%

list.title: Localized (early stage):
list.snippet: If lung cancer is found before it has spread outside the lung, the five-year survival rate can be as high as 67%.

list.title: Regional (spread to nearby lymph nodes):
list.snippet: If the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes, the five-year survival rate drops to around 33.5%.

list.title: Distant (spread to distant organs):
list.snippet: If the cancer has spread to distant parts of the body, the five-year survival rate is much lower, around 7%.

list.title: Overall (all stages combined):
list.snippet: The average five-year survival rate for all stages combined is around 26.6%.
